goal: Speeds up the CBlockIndexWorkComparator and arith_uint256 comparisons used when the node picks the best chain candidate.
Benefit is a faster CheckBlockIndex and slightly cheaper chain-candidate bookkeeping, mainly felt by developers running debug checks and by IBD/reorg-heavy workloads.

result.summary: This PR optimizes CBlockIndexWorkComparator (used to order block-index candidates) and the arith_uint256 comparison it relies on, replacing manual branchy comparisons with std::tie/std::strong_ordering and inlining hot functions. It adds a dedicated benchmark, deterministic unit tests, and differential fuzz targets comparing old and new comparator/comparison behavior for equivalence. Benchmarks show 1.4x-6.8x faster raw comparator throughput and roughly 1.4-1.6x faster CheckBlockIndex.
result.problem: The comparator is invoked heavily when maintaining setBlockIndexCandidates and in several ChainstateManager/Chainstate routines (FindMostWorkChain, ActivateBestChain, CheckBlockIndex, LoadBlockIndex, etc.), and profiling during investigation of issue #33618 showed it consuming a large share of CheckBlockIndex's time. Reviewers questioned how much this matters outside of CheckBlockIndex (mostly used in regtest/debug), so the real-world performance benefit for mainnet IBD/reorg workloads is not firmly established.

resolved_concerns: mzumsande's request for a differential fuzz test and comment clarity, addressed by adding fuzz targets and rewording comments (per l0rinc's pushes).
maflcko's suggestion to isolate the trivial move-only inline commit from the rest, addressed by reordering commits so the move-only change comes first.
optout21's nits on indentation and loop style, fixed in subsequent pushes.

categories.evidence: CBlockIndexWorkComparator is used directly in Chainstate::FindMostWorkChain, PruneBlockIndexCandidates, ActivateBestChain, InvalidateBlock, and ChainstateManager::LoadBlockIndex/CheckBlockIndex/ActivateSnapshot, all core validation hot paths, as the description details.

uncertainties: Whether the comparator speedup translates into a measurable real-world improvement for mainnet block connection/reorg performance, as opposed to only the CheckBlockIndex debug check, was raised by maflcko and not conclusively settled.

Whether this PR belongs more properly under a 'utils' style category for arith_uint256 changes was not asked, but arith_uint256.h changes are general-purpose and could also touch other consumers beyond block index comparisons.
result.card: This PR optimizes CBlockIndexWorkComparator and the underlying arith_uint256 comparison operator used throughout block-index candidate selection (setBlockIndexCandidates, ActivateBestChain, CheckBlockIndex, etc.), replacing manual comparisons with std::tie and C++20 spaceship operators plus inlining. Benchmarks show 1.4x-6.8x faster raw comparisons and about 1.4-1.6x faster CheckBlockIndex, with new unit tests, a benchmark, and differential fuzz targets proving equivalence with the old logic. Review is Ready: the latest push (2026-08-22) was re-ACKed with no open comments, and CI/mergeability are clean. Agreement is Strong, with ACKs from laanwj, optout21, and Raimo33, and mzumsande's and maflcko's concerns (fuzz coverage, comment clarity, commit ordering) resolved via follow-up pushes. The main open question, raised by maflcko, is whether the speedup meaningfully affects real-world (non-regtest) performance rather than just the CheckBlockIndex debug check.
